VENTO (NCT07201051, eligibility read 2026-11-16) enrols CT-confirmed bronchiectasis in current sputum producers with 2 or more exacerbations needing antibiotics or 1 needing hospitalisation in 12 months, or 0 to 1 exacerbation with a QOL-B respiratory symptom score under 50, FEV1 30% or more, primary asthma or COPD excluded. The exacerbation route is measured in the US Bronchiectasis and NTM Research Registry, 2,950 adults (Lapinel NC et al., ERJ Open Res 2024, doi 10.1183/23120541.00185-2024, PMID 39534769, PMC11551853, the source AZD0292's row cites): 438 had 2 exacerbations and 607 had 3 or more in the 2 years before enrolment. (438 + 607) / 2,950 = 0.354237
column12: JUDGEMENT on what is left out: the symptom-only route (QOL-B RSS under 50 with 0 or 1 exacerbation) has no free US share and is not counted, which understates; two exacerbations over two years is looser than two in one, and a specialist-centre registry is sicker than the claims pool, which both overstate. Not the AZD0292 eligible share, because CLEAR also requires Pseudomonas, so the two rows are different slices of one pool and pool_crowding keeps them apart

column12: no measured launch in this disease: Brinsupri (approved 2025-08-12, openFDA NDA217673) has too few months of CMS data to fit. The case for higher: VENTO enrols a broader group than CLEAR and a quarterly injection is a lighter burden than an infusion. The case for lower: Brinsupri is an oral tablet with a label and a head start of about eight years
